title: Pumpkin Spice Latte with Real Squash
changes_from_base: Milk simmered with butternut squash, maple syrup and warm spices, then blended smooth and poured over espresso instead of steamed plain milk; no latte art.
summary: A café latte made the cosy autumn way: instead of plain steamed milk, real butternut squash is simmered in milk with maple and warm spices, blended to a velvety foam and poured over espresso.
equipment: tea infuser ball or a small square of muslin and string
espresso machine, moka pot or cafetière

ingredients.item: butternut squash, peeled and cut into 2 cm cubes
fine sea salt or table salt
freshly made espresso (4 single shots) or very strong coffee

steps.title: Spice bundle
steps.text: Pack the cinnamon stick, star anise, cloves and cardamom into an infuser ball, or knot them in a square of muslin. Whole spices give a clean flavour, and the bundle saves you sieving later.

steps.title: Cook the squash
steps.text: Put the squash, milk, maple syrup, ginger, nutmeg and salt in a heavy pan with the spice bundle and bring it just to a simmer over medium heat. Lower the heat until the surface barely trembles and cook for 25-30 minutes, scraping the base every few minutes, until a cube collapses when pressed. Low heat matters: boiling milk scorches and can split.

steps.title: Blend
steps.text: Lift out the spice bundle. Blitz with a stick blender for about a minute, or in a jug blender with the lid vented and a tea towel on top, until silky and foamy; the squash starch is what gives the drink its body.

steps.title: Coffee
steps.text: Pull four single shots of espresso, or brew very strong coffee, and pour 30 ml into each mug.

steps.title: Pour
steps.text: Top each mug with 150-180 ml of the hot squash milk, give one stir and finish with a dusting of cinnamon.

tips: Don't let the milk boil hard while the squash cooks; it catches on the base and tastes burnt. Keep it at a bare simmer and scrape often.
Pumpkin works in place of butternut, but choose a sweet, dense variety.
Want it sweeter? Stir an extra teaspoon of maple into each mug rather than into the pan.
storage: Make the spiced squash milk up to 3 days ahead and keep it covered in the fridge. Reheat gently, stirring, until steaming, and blend again for foam. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
